Amanda — thanks for the clear questions. High level answers below; attaching a short playbook and a CSV sample of the audit logs for your team to review.

1) Region replication: By default, tenant volumes, snapshots, and backups for a "region-pinned" Dedicated instance remain in-region. Cross-region replication is opt-in and must be requested in writing as part of a defined DR/replication addendum. Any replication configuration is documented in the deployment configuration and the audit trail.

2) Deletion timeline (typical):
   - Primary purge from active hosts: infrastructure eviction and secure wipe initiated within 24–72 hours after a confirmed deletion request, dependent on scheduled maintenance windows.
   - Snapshot/backup destruction: snapshots are queued for destruction and reference-count swept within 7 days; if snapshots are subject to signed RPO agreements the timeline is extended per contract (we'll call that out in the addendum).
   - Logs/archival: access logs and audit exports are retained according to the contract default (90 days) unless FinTrust requests a shorter retention. Expedited deletion requests require an authenticated ticket and SOC‑approved handoff; typical expedited window is 5–10 business days depending on data locality and legal holds.

3) Failover behavior: Redwood's default failover policy for Dedicated is to prefer in-region replacement (evacuate to another host in the same AZ/region). Cross-region traffic routing is only used if the region experiences a sustained outage and an approved emergency failover policy is invoked by authorized FinTrust signatories. We will not spontaneously route customer traffic across regions without an explicit emergency escalation.

Please see attached: geo-containment-playbook.pdf (short ops summary) and audit-log-sample.csv (example of the event IDs you can expect).

If you want, Marissa can schedule a 30-min ops-to-ops handoff to walk the runbook and the escalation checklist.

Regards,

Amanda — adding some operational specifics you can include in your packet. Quoted short excerpt below (pulled from the attached playbook):

"Operational excerpt — containment and deletion
1) Instance pinning: upon provisioning an explicit 'region_pin' flag is set on the tenant record. All host leases, KV caches, and persistent volumes are constrained to hosts with the same region tag.

2) Snapshot lifecycle: snapshots are tagged with tenant_id + region. A background garbage collection process performs a two-phase sweep: mark (0–72 hours) then purge (up to 7 days). Purge includes cryptographic overwrite on ephemeral SSDs and de-referencing on object-store manifests.

3) Audit & attestation: for deletion events we produce a signed attestation that lists the resource ids, time of wipe, and the operator id. Those artifacts are delivered via secure link and stored for 180 days for audit purposes unless a shorter retention is requested.

Escalation & emergency failover
- Emergency failover requires two authorized FinTrust contacts plus our on-call lead to approve. In an emergency, traffic can be shifted to a cold-standby in another region, but data processing for new requests will only occur if FinTrust authorizes cross-region processing.

Operational contact: Marissa Cole (owner, Deployment Operations) — marissa_cole@redwood.com
